newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - MEHL says starts shipping.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - MEHL says starts shipping.

text.p: MEHL/Biophile International Corp said on Thursday it had begun shipping its hair-removal laser systems and expected to show income early next year.
"We'll start having an income the first quarter of '97," MEHL/Biophile chairman Thomas Mehl said in an interview. "Right now we're a start up company four months old."
The company was formed in June with the completion of the merger between Selvac Corp and Classy Lady by Mehl of Puerto Rico.

Mehl said the company expected to ship 30 to 35 Chromos 694 systems by the end of the year. Its majority-owned unit SLS/Biophile Ltd will begin producing 30 hair-removal laser systems a month beginning in January, the company said.

The machines are being shipped to countries including Austrailia, New Zealand, Thailand, Ireland and Great Britain, Mehl said. The company has filed for U.S. Food and Drug Administration clearance of the machines, which could come early next year.
The machines use a pulse laser system that removes unwanted hair.
Gainesville, Fla.-based MEHL/Biophile's laser hair-removal competitors include Thermolase Corp and Palomar Medical Technology Inc.
Mehl said MEHL/Biophile has about 200 letters of intent from potential licensing partners.

The company receives revenues based on licensing deals that include an up-front payment and a percentage of revenues generated by the hair-removal systems. Under the deals MEHL/Biophile receives a continuing percentage of revenues, or $15,000 per system per month, whichever is greater, the company said.
